long_biography.plain_text:
A family tree prompted Elisabeth Maxwell's sustained work on Holocaust remembrance. Researching her husband Robert's relatives for their children, she identified more than 300 who had been killed. She marked their names with gold stars on a folded chart, which she gave to Yad Vashem.

Maxwell also helped bring Nicholas Winton's rescue work to public attention. After seeing his scrapbook of children evacuated from Czechoslovakia, she sent enquiries to their former foster addresses and helped publicise his story. The resulting newspaper coverage and television appearances reunited Winton with people he had helped reach safety in Britain.
